lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Janderson Roberto Teixeira | Lesson 4 -- Bigger, Cheaper, Better

listenings.text: And now our weekly look at getting to the airport. We compared the three usual ways, and the results are not what most people expect. The train is by far the cheapest, at about a quarter of the price of a taxi, and on a normal weekday morning it is also the fastest. The bus is slightly cheaper than the train, but it is much slower and far less reliable, because it sits in the same traffic as everybody else. The taxi is the most convenient of the three, because it takes you from your door to the terminal with no walking at all, and it is by far the most expensive. Our conclusion is simple. If you are travelling alone with one bag, take the train. If you are three people with heavy luggage, the taxi is better value for money than it looks.

Hello, this is Nina calling about the two hotels. I have looked at both of them and I want to give you my honest opinion before you make up your mind. The first one is closer to the office, about ten minutes on foot, and the rooms are bigger. It is also considerably more expensive, and I think it is slightly overpriced for what it offers. The second one is thirty minutes away by train, the rooms are smaller, but it is much quieter and the breakfast is far better. The downside of the second one is the journey in the morning. So: the first is more convenient, the second is better value for money. Call me back and tell me which one you want.

extra_audio.text: Nina asks Janderson whether he has made up his mind about the two hotels. He answers that he has not, and that he wants to compare them one more time. Nina says the first hotel is more convenient but slightly overpriced. Janderson replies that the second one looks like better value for money, even with the longer journey. Nina agrees and tells him the only real downside is the train in the morning.

paras: Every traveller has the same argument with themselves at six in the morning: the train or the taxi. The taxi is the most convenient option by a long way. It takes you from your door to the terminal, you never carry a bag more than five metres, and on a quiet Sunday it is not much slower than the train.

The problem is the price and the traffic. A taxi costs roughly four times more than a train ticket, and on a normal weekday it is far less reliable, because it sits in the same jam as everybody else. On a bad morning the most expensive option is also the slowest one, which is the worst possible combination.

The train is cheaper, faster and more predictable. It leaves every ten minutes and it is never in a traffic jam. The downside is the walking. You carry your own luggage to the platform, up the stairs, and across the terminal at the other end, and that is a real cost if you are travelling with three bags or with a small child.

So the honest answer is that neither option is better in general. The train is better value for money for one person with one bag. The taxi is better for three people with heavy luggage, and it stops being overpriced the moment you divide it by three. The mistake is not choosing the taxi. The mistake is choosing it without comparing.
reading.source: Article -- a travel column in a weekend newspaper
